summary: A scholar in Buddhist and religious studies, Frank E. Reynolds served at the University of Chicago as Professor (~1967-2000) and later as Emeritus Professor (~2000-2019).

Frank Ernest Keay worked in Indology and religious studies, earning a B.A. (~1897-1900) and M.A. (~1914-1917) from the University of London. He served as Principal at Talghari Boys' School (1922) and priest at Bishop Cotton School (1941-1944).
Frank F. Conlon, a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology, studied at the University of Minnesota (1969). He later served as Professor Emeritus at the University of Washington (~2004).

Frank J. Hoffman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and under Stewart Sutherland, Eliot Deutsch, David J. Kalupahana, Prithwish Neogy, Rama Nath Sharma, and Kashi Nath Upadhyaya.
Working in religious studies and Indology, Frank J. Korom was a graduate student at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 1990) and became a Professor at Boston University (attested 2005).

Frank Lee Woodward studied at Christ's Hospital, Sidney Sussex College, and under Caroline Rhys Davids. Working in Buddhist studies and Indology, he held teaching posts in England, served as Dekan at Mahinda College (1903-1919), and translated for the Pali Text Society (~1919).

Frank Lillingston was an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his B.A. (~1891-1894) and M.A. (~1894-1898) at Pembroke College. He served as Theological Lecturer at Selwyn College (1897-1898).

Frank Raymond Allchin studied at the University of London and SOAS, completing his doctorate under K. de B. Codrington. An Indologist and archaeologist, he taught at SOAS (1954-1959) and the University of Cambridge (1959; 1972-1989), and co-founded the Ancient India and Iran Trust.

Frank Walter Nicolson studied at Mount Allison University (B.A. ~1879-1883) and Harvard University (A.B. ~1885-1887). He worked in Indology and classics, serving as Instructor in Sanskrit at Harvard (1888-1889) and Professor of Latin at Wesleyan University (1913-1934).
Frank Whittingham Skemp, active in Indology and linguistics, earned a B.A. from the University of Manchester (~1897-1900) and studied at Peterhouse (1903-1904) in preparation for the I.C.S.

Frank-Richard Hamm studied at Hamburg under Walther Schubring and others, and at the International Academy of Indian Culture. Active in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, he taught at Hamburg, held Berlin's chair of Indology (1964), and became Professor at Bonn (1965).

Franklin Edgerton studied at Cornell, Munich, Jena, and Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield. A scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies, he was Professor of Sanskrit at Pennsylvania (1913-1926) and Professor at Yale (1926-1953), also holding posts at Harvard and Banaras Hindu University.

Frans Wilhelm Gustaf Hjelt studied at the University of Helsinki and Uppsala University under Otto Fredrik Tullberg. Working in Indology, he held a post at the University of Helsinki (1844) and served as Rector at Turun Katedraalikoulu (1845-1872).
František Kamarýt was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Charles University, completing his Ph.D. under Josef Zubatý in 1917.

František Čupr studied at Charles University (Ph.D. ~1840-1845), where he became PD in 1849. Active in philosophy and Indology, he also taught at Akademické gymnázium v Praze (1848-1853) and served as principal of Prague First Private Czech Gymnasium (1853).

František Šohaj, an Indologist and linguist, earned his Ph.D. from Charles University by 1848. He served as Professor of Philosophy at Charles University (1848-1859) before taking a post at Akademické gymnázium v Praze in 1859.

Franz Altheim, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, earned his Ph.D. at Goethe University Frankfurt (1916-1921). He held academic posts at Frankfurt (PD 1928), Halle-Wittenberg (Professor 1936), and the Free University of Berlin (Professor 1950-1965).

Franz Aubrey Metcalf is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned a BA from UC Berkeley, an MA from the Graduate Theological Union, and a Ph.D. from the University of Chicago. He was an Instructor at California State University, Los Angeles in 1998.

Franz August Schmölders studied at Bonn (Ph.D. ~1829-1836) and Paris (~1836-1842). Active in Indology and philosophy, he was a PD at Humboldt University of Berlin (1842) and later held posts at Bonn (~1844-1846) and the University of Breslau (Professor 1846).

Franz Bernhard studied at Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt and Werner Thomas, and completed his habilitation at Frankfurt. Working in Indology and Buddhist studies, he held posts at Tübingen, Frankfurt (PD 1965), and the University of Hamburg (Professor 1966-1971).
